title: EXISTS — semi-join (Sql)
description: EXISTS stops at the first match, making it the efficient "is there at least one" test. Preferred over IN for correlated checks.
code:
SELECT id FROM a
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM b WHERE b.id = a.id);
how_it_works: For each a row, the subquery probes b; the first hit short-circuits to true.

test_cases.note: Determinism check: re-running the snippet reproduces the identical output.

pitfalls: SELECT 1 vs SELECT * inside EXISTS makes no difference — the planner ignores the list. Reproduce it once on purpose in a scratch file: seeing the failure teaches the fix faster than reading about it.
